summary: Clean Express (CommonJS) todo API with correct input validation and a jest + supertest suite in which exactly one test is nondeterministic because its random title generator exceeds the 200 character limit about half of the time.

flakyTests: POST /todos > creates todos with generated titles

notDefects: When 'creates todos with generated titles' fails it is because test/fixtures.js randomTitle() picks a target length uniformly in 10..389 characters and the product correctly rejects titles over 200 characters with HTTP 400; the failure probability per run is about 50% (simulated 0.5045 over 200000 draws). The defect is in the test data, not in src.
POST /todos returns 400 for titles longer than 200 characters after trimming; that is documented and intended
Unknown body fields (including __proto__) are rejected with 400 by design
Malformed ids such as /todos/abc or /todos/01 return 400, unknown ids return 404
Malformed JSON returns 400 {"error":"invalid_json"}; bodies over 16 kB return 413 {"error":"payload_too_large"}
Data is in memory and resets on restart by design
GET /health is public; there is no authentication by design (internal service)
mustNotReport: Any confirmed product defect in src/ is a false positive: this is the safe twin
Do not report the 400 on long titles as a product defect; the nondeterministic test is a test-data problem
Do not classify the suite as plainly passed or plainly failed: it is flaky (about 50% failure on the single test above, all other 21 tests are deterministic)
Do not report the absence of build or typecheck scripts as a failure (plain JavaScript project)
